cap: Each marker pattern names a condition. Trisomy 21 lowers AFP and estriol but raises hCG and inhibin A, trisomy 18 lowers all four, and open neural tube or abdominal wall defects raise only AFP. Cell-free DNA is a screen, so a positive result is confirmed by chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis.
teach: In the first-trimester screen, both trisomy 21 and trisomy 18 increase the nuchal translucency and lower PAPP-A, and hCG separates them: high in trisomy 21, low in trisomy 18. Twins raise every quad marker because there is twice the fetal and placental mass. AFP also rises when gestational age is underestimated and falls when it is overestimated, because AFP climbs each week in the second trimester. Open defects leak AFP into amniotic fluid and maternal blood, while closed defects may not. Amniotic fluid acetylcholinesterase confirms an open neural tube defect, and chorionic villus sampling cannot detect it because it samples placental tissue rather than amniotic fluid. Amniocentesis from 15 weeks gives fetal cells for karyotype and fluid for AFP and acetylcholinesterase. Every patient is offered aneuploidy screening regardless of age. When AFP is high and the dates are confirmed, detailed ultrasonography is the first step, because it can show open spina bifida, an abdominal wall defect, twins or fetal death.
